title: HistoricalEventEnvelope
description: Envelope of every Historical Event (HSE section 12, ADR-0014). A historical event is NOT a domain event: it is a record the history engine made because a significance rule judged one or more committed domain events historically significant (principle 4). It has no sequence, correlation_id or causation_id - its order and its cause are its source_event_ids. It has NO free-text narrative field: headlines and sentences are built by the presentation layer from event_type + payload (principle 2 and 6, HSE section 105). Type-specific facts ('what') live in payload; generic 'who' and 'where' live here so that later projections can query across types. Type schemas compose this with allOf and close the object with unevaluatedProperties:false.

historical_event_id.description: Deterministic id derived from the record's meaning: UUIDv5(NS_HISTORY, '{world_id}|{event_type}|{dedupe_key}') with NS_HISTORY = 29c482cc-234d-4876-a837-347b852f802d (ADR-0014 section 1). Rebuilding history from domain_events reproduces the same id, so the client's duplicate filter (LIVE vs BACKFILL) and later Claims can reference it.

rule_version.description: Rule that produced this record. Never recomputed when the rule changes.

importance_level.description: HSE section 11: 1 Local, 2 Regional, 3 Political, 4 Galactic, 5 Epoch-defining. Level 0 (Ephemeral) means 'not historical' and therefore can never be stored or sent (spec p1-02 I-60). Fixed at creation by the rule; a later rise in significance is a projection, not an edit of this record.

tick.description: Tick of the decisive source domain event.

occurred_at.description: Game time of the decisive source domain event.

recorded_at.description: Real time the history runner committed this record. Audit only; excluded from determinism comparisons.

source_event_ids.description: Committed domain events this record was judged from, in (tick, sequence) order. Every id exists in domain_events (spec p1-02 I-62).

participants.description: Who took part, each with a role. Generic across event types so that a biography can later ask 'every record this actor or ship appears in' without knowing each payload.

Visibility.title: Visibility
Visibility.description: Who may know this record exists (historical-engine skill section 5). Visibility is not the same as evidence existing. p1-02 produces only PUBLIC for events (PARTICIPANTS_ONLY appears on evidence, which is DB-only). Closed set that may grow: consumers treat an unknown value as not displayable and keep running.

FactStatus.title: FactStatus
FactStatus.description: State of the FACT, never of its interpretation (HSE section 13). CONFIRMED = the server observed it directly. Locked to one value by a DB CHECK; adding a value is a migration plus an ADR (ADR-0014 section 3).

entity_kind.description: PLAYER = an actor (character; GDD section 4). SHIP = a ship entity; ships are not persisted (ADR-0011 section 7), so a SHIP participant is the only lasting trace of which hull was there. Closed set that may grow.

role.description: DISCOVERER (the PLAYER who made a discovery), VESSEL (the SHIP it was made with). Closed set that may grow.
